whatToTest:
New: start Tend with Siri and keep it on the Lock Screen.

1. Say "Hey Siri, start Tend" (or "trigger Tend"). Siri asks "What are you working on?". Say your question, like "read this paper and find out how metabolic pathways simplify things". The session starts without opening the app.
2. Lock the phone: your question, the pixel tomato and the countdown are on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island. The ring empties and the tomato ripens while you work. Try Pause, Resume and Done there.
3. When the time is up (or after Done), press and hold the "A moment to gather" notification and type or dictate where you stopped. Open Tend: the session and your note are in the Notebook, and the note is offered as your next question.
4. Also try "Hey Siri, pause Tend", "resume Tend" and "I'm done in Tend" (Siri asks where you stopped).
5. Tend's actions are in the Shortcuts app, so you can put "Start a session" on the Action Button or on Back Tap (Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Back Tap).

Sessions you start inside Tend show on the Lock Screen too.
whatsNew:
Start a session with Siri: say "Start Tend", tell it your question, and the session begins without opening the app. Add a length if you like: "read this paper for 50 minutes", or "plank 90 seconds" for a quick timer.

Your session now lives on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island: the question, the pixel tomato and the countdown, with Pause and Done.

When the time is up, leave a note on where you stopped right from the notification. It waits in your notebook as the next question.

Block distracting apps while you focus: pick them once in Settings, and they stay locked until the session ends or you tap Done.

Tend's actions are in the Shortcuts app too. "Start a focus session" hands on its end time, so a shortcut can keep Do Not Disturb on until you're done.
reviewNotes:
New in 1.1, Siri and the Lock Screen (no account or setup needed):
1. Say "Start Tend" to Siri, or run Tend > Start a session in the Shortcuts app. Siri asks "What are you working on?"; answer with anything. The session starts without opening the app.
2. Lock the device: a Live Activity shows the question, the tomato and the countdown on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island, with Pause/Resume and Done buttons.
3. When the time is up, or after Done, the "A moment to gather" notification offers "Leave a note" with a text field (press and hold it). The note appears in Tend's Notebook.
4. "Pause Tend", "Resume Tend" and "I'm done in Tend" also work with Siri.
5. A length in the answer sets the session: "plank 90 seconds" starts a 90-second quick timer, which ends without a reflection.
6. Optional app blocking (Screen Time): Settings > Block apps while you focus > Choose apps. Tend asks for Screen Time permission (FamilyControls, individual authorization) and shows Apple's FamilyActivityPicker. During a focus session the chosen apps are shielded with a "Tend is on" screen; pausing, tapping Done or the end of the session lifts it. Tend keeps only the picker's opaque tokens, on the device. It is a self-control tool for the device's own user.

Everything stays on the device; no data is collected.

testflight.3:
New in build 3: quick timers and Do Not Disturb.

1. Say "Hey Siri, start Tend", then answer with a length: "plank 90 seconds", or "read this paper for 50 minutes". Under 5 minutes is a quick timer: it counts down on the Lock Screen and buzzes at the end, without asking where you stopped or going into your notebook. Your research question stays as it was.
2. Do Not Disturb: in the Shortcuts app, make a new shortcut with Tend's "Start a focus session", then "Set Focus": Do Not Disturb, Turn On, Until: Time, and pick the time Tend hands over. Name it "Tend focus". "Hey Siri, Tend focus" then starts a session and keeps the phone quiet until it ends. It fits the Action Button too.
3. The time's up notice is Time Sensitive now, so it still reaches you in Do Not Disturb.

Everything from build 2 is still here: Siri start, the Lock Screen timer, Pause and Done, and the "Where did you stop?" note.
testflight.4:
New in build 4: block apps while you focus.

1. Open Tend > Settings (the sliders, top right) > Block apps while you focus > Choose apps. iOS asks once for Screen Time permission (your passcode), then shows Apple's app list. Pick the apps or categories that pull you away (Tend never learns which ones; Apple only hands it anonymous tokens).
2. Say "Trigger Tend" and answer the question as usual. While the session runs, the apps you picked show a dark "Tend is on" screen with the pixel tomato.
3. Pause, Done, or the timer running out unlocks them. Breaks and quick timers ("plank 90 seconds") don't block anything.
4. Try it with the phone locked: start with Siri, open a blocked app, then tap Done on the Lock Screen and open it again.

Everything from builds 2 and 3 is still here.

build_note: "build" is the one asc-submit.mjs submits (Houfu tested build 4's app blocking on his iPhone, 2026-10-27: "nice it works"); "testflight" holds What to Test for TestFlight builds.
